newsitem.title: CANADA: Westcoast deal seen geared for competition.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast deal seen geared for competition.

text.p: Westcoast Energy Inc's incentive toll deal with natural gas producers in British Columbia, announced on Wednesday, will help the pipeline firm deal with growing competition on its home turf, a Canadian producer official said.

"What we're contemplating with this arrangement is adapting the regulatory framework to a strengthening competitive environment," Nick Schultz, general counsel for the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers, said in a phone interview.
Vancouver-based Westcoast, the main mover of gas in British Columbia, on Wednesday said it and CAPP had struck a deal for an incentive-based rate strucuture for shippers.
The agreement, which is still only in principle, would make it the last major pipeline firm in Canada to establish such a structure with its customers.

"They have a more complex system (than other firms) because they have gathering and processing as well as transmission," Schultz said. "Gathering and processing has been the most difficult issue to deal with."

Over the past two years, new players to British Columbia gathering and processing -- notably NOVA Corp affiliate Novagas Clearinghouse Ltd -- have threatened to sway customers from Westcoast and move gas production east into Alberta, bypassing British Columbia's biggest system.

Schultz said Westcoast and CAPP expected to have the major details of the arrangement hammered out before the end of the first quarter and the longer-term regulatory aspects finalized before the end of 1997.
"It's a framework agreement, so there are a number of details to be worked through," he said.
Other stakeholders who still must be brought to the negotiating table include gas utilities in Canada and the United States as well as other industrial customers.
